text: I'm assembling a reporter plasmid (lac promoter -> sfGFP -> rrnB T1 terminator, the region I care about is ~1.5 kb) and I keep losing track of what's where in a plain text file. can you make a page that shows the sequence in rows of 60 with the position number at the start of each row, lets me drag across bases with the mouse and mark that stretch as a promoter, CDS, terminator or primer site, and draws the features as coloured bars above the sequence like snapgene does. make up a ~1500bp placeholder sequence for now, I'll paste mine in later

need a list of the features too, with start, end, length and strand, where I can fix the coordinates by typing and delete the ones I got wrong. coords 1-based and inclusive like genbank please. and I need to set the strand when I mark something, the terminator and one of the primers are on the minus strand

can you add a box to search for a motif? exact match is fine but it has to look on both strands, I'm checking that my M13 rev primer doesnt also sit somewhere on the bottom strand. highlight the hits and tell me which strand each one is on
show GC% for whatever I have selected, and if it's primer length a rough Tm too. showing the reverse complement of the selection would help for the minus strand primers
colours are a bit loud, can they be more muted. also when two features overlap the bars draw on top of each other and I can't click the lower one, stack them instead

export the features as a gff-like table, tab separated so I can paste it into our lab sheet. and add the place to paste my real sequence, it'll come from a genbank ORIGIN block so strip the numbers and spaces. and keep my features when I close the tab, lost them yesterday
